questions.question:
In the following question, select the related word pair from the given alternatives.

**Perimeter : Hexagon : : ? : ?**
questions.solution:
Sum of the sides of Hexagon is known as Perimeter. Similarly, sum of the sides of Rhombus is also known as Perimeter.

Note: Here on RHS geometrical shape is given. In case of Circle : Circumference, Circle is given on LHS. So cannot be the correct option.

Thus the related pair is Perimeter : Rhombus.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the related number from the given alternatives.

**45 : 20 : : 46 : ?**
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

45 → 4 × 5 = 20

Similarly,

46 → 4 × 6 = 24

Thus 46 is related to 24.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the related letter/letters from the given alternatives.

**IMO : PTV : : KOQ : ?**
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

I + 7 = P

M + 7 = T

O + 7 = V

Similarly,

K + 7 = R

O + 7 = V

Q + 7 = X

Thus, KOQ is related to RVX.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd word pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

On LHS class of animal is given and on RHS animal belonging to that class is given.

But in Crocodile - Reptile, on LHS animal is given and on RHS his class.

Thus, the pair Crocodile - Reptile is the odd word pair.

questions.question:
​In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

**6578, 4381, 2653, ?, 322**
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

6578 - 4381 = 2197 = 13³

4381 - 2653 = 1728 = 12³

So the next number should have difference of 1331 = 11³

So 2653 - 1331 = **1322**

That is, 2653 - 1322 = 1331

1322 - 322 = 1000 = 10³

Thus, the missing number is 1322.

questions.question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

**FH, KM, PR, UW,?**
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

F + 5 = K, K + 5 = P, P + 5 = U, U + 5 = Z

H + 5 = M, M + 5 = R, R + 5 = W, W + 5 = B

Thus, the next term in the series is ZB.

questions.question: Six boys are sitting in a row facing south. Gaurav is second to the right of Akash who is at one of the end. Prem is at fourth position to the left of Raman. Jatin and Nitin sit together. How many boys are sitting to the left of Nitin?
questions.solution:
Six boys are sitting in a row facing south.

1) Gaurav is second to the right of Akash who is at one of the end.

**Right** **End** _ _ _ Gaurav _ Akash **Left End**

2) Prem is at fourth position to the left of Raman.

**Right** **End** Raman _ _ Gaurav Prem Akash **Left End**

3) Jatin and Nitin sit together.

**Right** **End** Raman Jatin/Nitin Gaurav Prem Akash **Left End**

As the positon of Jatin is not confirm, we cannot determine the number of boys that are sitting to the left of Nitin.

questions.question: In a certain code language, “**CAB**” is written as “**6**” and “**LAN**” is written as “​**27**”. How is “**FAN**” written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

CAB = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6

LAN = 12 + 1 + 14 = 27

Similarly,

FAN = 6 + 1 + 14 = 21

Thus, FAN is coded as 21.

questions.question:
In the question two statements are given, followed by two conclusions, I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements.

**Statement** I: All pancakes are bread

**Statement** II: Some pizzas are pancakes

**Conclusion** I: No bread are pizzas

**Conclusion** II: Some pizzas are bread

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/424f25932ac3409168ec82789d241efecd344d7085b6d0f480e41e6e62a05634.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. No bread are pizzas → False (all those pizzas that are pancakes are bread)

II. Some pizzas are bread → True (all those pizzas that are pancakes are bread)

Thus, only statement II follows.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

**29, 27, 24, ?, 15, 9**
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

29 - 2 = 27,

27 - 3 = 24,

**24 - 4 = 20,**

20 - 5 = 15,

15 - 6 = 9

Thus, the missing number in the series is 20.

questions.question: In the following question, four groups of three numbers are given. In each group the second and third number are related to the first number by a Logic/Rule/Relation. Three are similar on basis of same Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the odd one out from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

4 + 9 = 13 and 13 + 4 = 17

6 + 9 = 15 and 15 + 4 = 19

**15 + 10 = 25 and 25 + 3 = 28**

11 + 9 = 20 and 20 + 4 = 24

Hence, (15, 28, 25) is the odd one out.
